To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the C282Y allele is present in 5% of ethnic Danes, the H63D and the S65C alleles in 13% and 2%, respectively.
the HFE variant genotypes C282Y and H63D were associated with elevated iron status markers in a Danish male population.
alcohol and meat consumption enhance the expression of the HFE gene variants C282Y, and H63D in men, whereas blood donation and milk consumption have a protective effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic and environmental factors affecting iron homeostasis and the development of iron overload.
the identification of the most relevant factors that influence the phenotypic manifestation of HFE variants.
the role of the HFE C282, H63, S65 gene variants in the development of iron overload and liver disease in a Danish population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HFE genotype has a higher impact than the extrinsic factors on iron status markers in Danish men.
HFE genotype and lifestyle factors interact to determine iron status in men.

the HFE genotype is a major risk factor for elevated iron status markers, and that alcohol and meat consumption are risk factors for elevated serum iron, serum ferritin, and transferrin saturation in Danish men.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HFE gene variant phenotype in Danish men was modified by a number of factors, but in particular by alcohol consumption and blood donation.
extrinsic factors have an important impact on the phenotypical expression of HFE variant alleles.
the HFE genotype is the most important factor in the development of iron overload, but that the expression of the genotype may be modulated by extrinsic factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the HFE variants have the highest impact on the expression of the iron phenotype, but that other factors such as age, alcohol, meat and milk consumption, egg consumption, and blood donation are also of importance in the expression of the HFE phenotype.
the HFE variants do not explain the majority of the variation in iron status in the Danish population.
the C282Y, C282Y, and C282Y/H63D phenotypes in men with normal iron status markers are associated with a high probability of elevated iron status markers.
